title: First working app
one_line_goal: One window browses websites safely: address bar, back, forward, refresh
summary: Build the first real Ferrum: a trusted shell around one website view, with safe navigation and a locked bridge so websites cannot call the app.

tasks.title: Build local test pages
tasks.chain: Real websites change → a local server with fixed pages (redirects, pop-ups, cookies, slow and error pages) → navigation tests give the same answer every run.
tasks.check: Server tests pass; each test page returns its documented status.

tasks.title: Create the desktop app
tasks.chain: The design was fixed in P1 → create the app with the chosen Tauri version and hosting route → the shell window opens.
tasks.check: Release build succeeds; the window shows the shell (screenshot saved).

tasks.title: Lock the bridge to the app
tasks.chain: Every web view can reach the app's command channel → grant permissions to the shell only, none to websites → a website cannot control Ferrum.
tasks.check: A test page tries app, plugin and event calls; every one is refused and logged.

tasks.title: Settings model
tasks.chain: Start page, navigation rules and data folder must be valid → typed settings with safe defaults → bad settings never crash or weaken the app.
tasks.check: Tests: valid file, missing file, bad address, non-HTTPS start page.

tasks.title: Clean up address-bar input
tasks.chain: People type anything → one tested function turns input into a safe address or refuses it → malformed input never navigates.
tasks.check: One test per input type (no scheme, http, foreign letters, IPv6, script, data and file links, junk) passes.

tasks.title: Show a website and track it
tasks.chain: The shell must know where the page is → create the website view and report address and loading state → the address bar and spinner are always right.
tasks.check: A test visits two pages; the shell receives address and load events in order.

tasks.title: Back, forward, refresh
tasks.chain: Basic browsing → use the method chosen in P1 and grey out buttons that cannot work → behaves like a normal browser.
tasks.check: A then B: back shows A, forward shows B, refresh reloads B; buttons match history.

tasks.title: Loading and error screens
tasks.chain: Pages are slow or fail → spinner and error panel drawn by the shell, never by loading the app's own pages into the website view → clear feedback without weakening security.
tasks.check: Slow, 404, 500 and unreachable tests each show the right state.

tasks.title: Follow redirects correctly
tasks.chain: Sites redirect → show the final address and stop loops with an error → the address bar never lies.
tasks.check: Each redirect test shows the final address; the loop test ends in an error.

tasks.title: New windows and outside links
tasks.chain: Links open new windows or other apps such as mail → follow the setting, and ask before handing off to another app → nothing launches without your consent.
tasks.check: The new-window test follows the setting; the mail-link test asks and launches nothing without consent.

tasks.title: Keep cookies across restarts
tasks.chain: Logins should survive a restart → keep site data in a fixed local folder → you stay signed in.
tasks.check: A test sets a cookie, restarts the app, and the cookie comes back.

tasks.title: Developer tools only in test builds
tasks.chain: Developer tools expose page internals → enable them only in debug builds → the release app stays locked.
tasks.check: The release build cannot open them; the debug build can.

tasks.title: Google sign-in: offer the normal browser
tasks.chain: Google may refuse sign-in inside embedded views → detect its sign-in page and offer the system browser, never disguise the app → we respect Google's rules.
tasks.check: Test on recorded addresses; a test link shows the banner. No live Google login.

tasks.title: Structured logs, no crashes
tasks.chain: Problems need evidence → Machine-readable log lines and clear errors, no crashing on bad navigation → failures can be diagnosed.
tasks.check: Every log line can be read by a program; no crash entries.

tasks.title: Quick whole-app tests
tasks.chain: Features interact → one suite drives shell and website view (Playwright if experiment 4 passed, otherwise Rust tests plus a manual list) → one command shows the first milestone works.
tasks.check: The suite command passes; output saved.

tasks.title: Update docs and part pages
tasks.chain: Code changed → README, security notes, known limits and part pages updated with the verified commit → docs match reality.
tasks.check: Wiki check clean; shell, web-view manager and core pages marked built.

tasks.title: Literature batch 2
tasks.chain: Research runs alongside code → read on WebView2 and Chromium processes, page lifecycle and embedded-view resource studies → evidence for later experiments.
tasks.check: New dated notes; the reading log is updated; no unchecked citation.

tasks.title: Run the gate; your review
tasks.chain: All tasks done → run every check and save the output → you try the release build and approve the first milestone.
tasks.check: All evidence saved; wiki clean; you approved the P2 exit.

test_gate.explanation: Every website view can reach the app's channel → first prove websites are refused, then prove navigation with small tests, quick whole-app tests and a release build → you try it on real sites → only then do tabs start in P3.

rows.proves: Dependencies are allowed and have no open alerts.
Shell style, types and tests pass.
The app you would ship builds.

Navigation, errors, redirects, links, cookies and the sign-in banner work.
